To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we isolated nine human monoclonals against a cluster of conformational epitope on HCV E1 that neutralized all genotypes of HCV with varying profiles and inhibited E2 binding of CD81.

we isolated a panel of human monoclonal neutralizing antibodies to a novel cluster of conformational epitope on HCV E1 and E2 glycoproteins, designated as antigen domain D, and that these antibodies are resistant to escape by HCV.
we isolated nine human monoclonals that neutralized HCV of genotypes 1 to 6.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of broadly neutralizing human monoclonal anti HCV antibodies.
the identification of broadly neutralizing monoclonal antibodies to HCV.
the development of a universal vaccine against HCV.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HC 84 HmAbs neutralize HCV by binding to a cluster of conformational epitope on HCV E1/E2, which is distinct from the antigenic domain B and is highly resistant to neutralization escape.

this study identified a cluster of conformational epitope on HCV E 2 that are highly conserved across genotypes and mediate broad virus neutralization and are not susceptible to neutralization escape.
the HC 84 HmAbs neutralize HCV by targeting a novel antigenic domain on the E2 protein that includes two regions of the E2 protein, aa 418 446 and 611 616.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the antigenic domains A, B and D, which are all highly conserved, are relevant for a vaccine that elicits broad virus neutralizing antibodies.
a cluster of conformational epitope(s) in antigenic domain B on E2 is the major site for neutralizing antibodies in the human response to HCV.
the HC 84 H2 and HC 84 H3 antibodies are the first human monoclonal antibody that neutralize all HCV genotypes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have isolated human monoclonal antibody (HMAb) that neutralize HCV with genotypes 2a 6a.
we isolated a novel group of broadly neutralizing HMAbs that recognize an epitope that is not neutralization escape prone.
the antigenic domain D on HCV E1/E2 is a highly immunogenic site that elicits antibodies with broad neutralization profiles and that are resistant to escape in HCVcc passaging.
